leads.name: Washington Square Oaks
leads.reason: Square in the Oakleigh Garden Historic District (NRHP 1972, Washington Square deeded to city 1850); the district's live oak canopies planted 1850 to 1910 per the nomination (search summary, not fetched). One source, no per-tree facts, no oak count seen. Next step: NPS nomination PDF at npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/005589a9-148e-4060-a8d3-d5c62cc07509 and Mobile Bay Magazine Ask McGehee on Washington Square (p=29099, 403 to fetch).

leads.name: Spring Hill College Avenue of the Oaks (Stewartfield)
leads.reason: Avenue of about 50 live oaks planted about 1850 by Roger Stewart; campus access for the public unconfirmed, and an avenue is not one collectible point. Needs a source for open campus and a standout trunk before it can ship.

leads.name: Government Street oaks (Oakleigh Garden District)
leads.reason: Tree Trail brochure claims British forces planted oaks along Government Street 1736 to 1780: uncorroborated, avenue, not recorded as a tree.

blocked.name: Jury Oak, Historic Blakeley State Park
blocked.reason: Park visitor guide describes a pavilion preserving the remains of the Jury Oak, so the tree is gone; a separate live oak at the Old House Site is unnamed and unmeasured.

blocked.name: Avenue of the Oaks, Spring Hill College
blocked.reason: Avenue, not a collectible point; see lead for the possible standout trunk.
